propositions: The test fails intermittently when two concurrent writers call git add and commit in an interleaved sequence, because the add/commit pair is not serialized despite each individual call holding an advisory lock.

When alpha adds and commits while beta has already added, alpha's bare git commit sweeps the entire index including beta's staged changes, leaving beta with nothing to commit and rc=1 with empty stderr.
The test's assertion of returncode==0 for both writers asserts a guarantee the product never made: that two whole-index commits are both non-empty.
Fixing the test requires each worker to commit only its own pathspec rather than the whole index, so a writer losing the add/commit interleaving still has its own change to commit.

The test's failure reporting discards git stdout (which contains the diagnostic message) and the command name, making failures non-self-diagnosing; assertions must include both stdout and stderr plus command identity.
No product code defect exists; the contention seam and lock policy are correct, and git behaves correctly in all scenarios.
